drafts.title: Preserve and strengthen engaging drivetrain and handling character
drafts.description: Customers experience lively, immediate acceleration and confident, precise handling that make daily driving and spirited driving feel engaging and controllable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized handling test (skidpad) the vehicle should achieve a sustained lateral acceleration of at least 0.95 g and in straight-line acceleration achieve 0–60 mph in 5.5 seconds or less for the standard performance level; in a blinded user drive test >=85% of participants rate driving dynamics as 'engaging' (top-2 on 5-point scale).
assumptions: Current G60 baseline is approximately 0.90 g on the skidpad and ~5.8 s 0–60 mph for comparable trim; targets assume incremental improvement possible within 3–5 years.
Standardized test procedures and participant panels are consistent with internal BMW test methodology.
uncertainties: Exact baseline values for all current variants may vary; electric vs hybrid variants will differ in mass and performance.
Customer perception of 'engaging' driving may shift with new competitors or EV driving characteristics.
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-facing driving dynamics and perceived engagement are in scope for successor vehicle requirements.

drafts.title: Maintain high ride comfort and spacious cabin impression
drafts.description: Customers feel the ride is supple and comfortable across real-world road conditions and perceive the cabin as spacious and relaxing for driver and passengers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 2-hour real-world comfort study with a representative panel, >=85% of participants rate overall ride comfort top-2 on a 5-point scale and >=85% rate rear-seat spatial impression top-2.
assumptions: Test panel reflects target US customer demographics for the 5 Series.
Real-world test routes include a mix of urban, suburban and highway surfaces.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort can be affected by seat tuning vs. suspension trade-offs and customer preferences across markets.
drafts.scope_reason: Keeping and refining perceived ride comfort and cabin space is a customer outcome for the successor vehicle.

drafts.title: Reduce seat-related complaints by improving adjustability and long-distance comfort
drafts.description: Customers find the seats comfortable for long trips and able to be adjusted to their body shapes, reducing complaints about firmness, support or fit.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a 3-hour long-drive study, seat-related complaints measured via standardized questionnaire must be reduced by at least 60% compared to the current G60 baseline and >=80% of participants rate seat comfort top-2 on a 5-point scale.
assumptions: Current G60 seat complaint rate will be measured by the same questionnaire to create a valid baseline.
Improvements will come from changes in cushion geometry, support zones and adjustability rather than only materials.
uncertainties: Some seat preferences are highly personal; reducing complaints by 60% may require multiple seat options or package choices.
drafts.scope_reason: Seat comfort and adjustability are direct customer-facing aspects that must be addressed in the successor.

drafts.title: Reliable hands-free trunk opening and dependable Comfort Access lock/unlock
drafts.description: Customers can open the trunk with a foot gesture and lock/unlock the vehicle reliably with keyless Comfort Access without repeated failures or the need to use the key fob manually.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Foot-gesture trunk opening success rate >=95% over 200 varied real-world attempts (different footwear, lighting and approach angles) with false-trigger rate <=1%; Comfort Access lock/unlock failure rate <=1% over 1000 simulated approach/departure events.
assumptions: Test attempts will include representative customer behaviors that caused complaints in current fleet.
Environmental conditions include rain, low light and covered/garage approaches.
uncertainties: Certain edge cases (very cold conditions, heavy interference from other key fobs) may still cause rare failures.
Hardware placement constraints could affect gesture sensing performance.
drafts.scope_reason: Improving Comfort Access and trunk usability is a direct customer requirement for the next-generation vehicle.

drafts.title: Deliver a significantly improved electric driving range and practical DC charging experience
drafts.description: Customers experience a usable electric range suitable for daily and extended driving and can recharge quickly in typical public DC charging scenarios so electric ownership is convenient.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For the BEV variant, EPA-equivalent single-charge electric range >=300 miles; in common public DC charging conditions (150 kW-class chargers) charge from 10% to 80% in 25 minutes or less; in owner-reported charging logs, range-related complaints decrease by at least 50% vs current G60 ownership data.
assumptions: Successor will offer BEV variants with battery and weight optimizations enabling ~300 mile range within 3–5 years.
Sufficient public DC chargers with 150 kW capability will be available on typical routes in target markets.
EPA-equivalent range is the primary customer-communicated metric in the US.
uncertainties: Real-world range varies with temperature, towing, payload and user driving style; fleet-wide complaint reduction depends on educating customers about range expectations.
Public charger reliability and power availability remain outside vehicle control and can affect customer experience.
drafts.scope_reason: Electric range and perceived charging convenience are core customer outcomes for the successor vehicle.

drafts.title: Make public charging easy to find and use by integrating reliable charger status and routing
drafts.description: Customers can plan trips with confidence because the vehicle suggests chargers that are likely to be available and routes that include working chargers without excessive detours or failed charge attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Routing suggestions must prioritize chargers with historical or live uptime >=90% and offer alternatives such that the added detour time does not exceed 15 minutes for 90% of routed charging stops; successful public-charging session failures (unable to charge due to station issues) are reduced by >=80% in owner logs compared to current baseline.
assumptions: Access to live and historical third-party charger data is available via partnerships or reliable aggregator APIs.
Map and routing updates are delivered to the vehicle with sufficient frequency to reflect station status.
uncertainties: Third‑party networks may not provide uniform uptime data; differences in regional coverage will affect performance.
Live data accuracy depends on third-party reporting and network connectivity.
drafts.scope_reason: Customer-facing charging navigation and station reliability information is in scope to improve charging experience.

drafts.title: Keep the touchscreen and operating concept intuitive while reducing usability complaints
drafts.description: Customers can operate the primary functions via the touchscreen and system menus intuitively without confusion, and overall touchscreen usability issues are reduced while preserving the positive aspects users like today.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a representative usability study, touchscreen/menu dissatisfaction falls to <=5% and top-2 overall satisfaction with the operating concept reaches >=80%; average task completion time for common tasks (navigation destination entry, climate quick-adjust) is <12 seconds with <=2 errors.
assumptions: Usability study methods and participant selection align with the referenced US study approach.
Improvements can be delivered through software UI changes, logical menu restructuring and selective physical controls for frequent tasks.
uncertainties: Balancing advanced features with simplicity may require multiple UI modes or personalization to satisfy all user groups.
Software updates post-launch may be needed to tune real-world behavior.
drafts.scope_reason: Improving the infotainment operating concept and touchscreen usability is a product design objective for the next-generation vehicle.

drafts.title: Provide reliable wireless phone connectivity and dependable in-car wireless charging
drafts.description: Customers can use wireless Apple CarPlay and other phone integrations reliably, and wireless charging consistently charges popular phone models without frequent dropouts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Wireless CarPlay connects successfully on the first attempt >=98% across a test matrix of major phone models; wireless charging supports and actively charges >=95% of tested popular phone models (with common cases) such that phones maintain or increase state-of-charge during typical drives, and incidents of dropped CarPlay sessions are <=2% over 1000 connection-hours.
assumptions: Test matrix includes representative iOS and popular Android devices used by target customers in the US and common protective cases.
Vehicle OTA updates can address compatibility issues post-launch.
uncertainties: Rapidly changing phone hardware and OS updates may create new incompatibilities after launch.
Magnetic phone mounts and aftermarket accessories could reduce charging reliability.
drafts.scope_reason: Phone connectivity and reliable wireless charging are customer-facing features to be improved in the successor vehicle.

drafts.title: Improve instrument cluster clarity and reduce related usability complaints
drafts.description: Drivers receive clear, relevant information from the instrument cluster without distraction or confusing transitions, improving perceived clarity and reducing instrument-cluster-related complaints.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a driving study, instrument cluster legibility and non-distracting behavior must achieve top-2 rating by >=85% of participants and instrument-cluster-related complaints in owner feedback drop to <=3% of reported infotainment/cluster issues.
assumptions: Driver studies are conducted under representative lighting and traffic conditions.
Cluster information density and animation choices are tuned with human factors input.
uncertainties: Some drivers prefer more information while others want minimal displays; personalization options may be required.
drafts.scope_reason: Instrument cluster usability is a direct customer-facing attribute to address in the next vehicle.

drafts.title: Make climate controls and quick adjustments intuitive and reachable
drafts.description: Customers can change temperature, fan and defogging settings quickly without navigating deep menus or taking attention from the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a timed usability test, users must be able to change cabin temperature by ±2°C and adjust fan level within 3 seconds and no more than 2 interactions in >=90% of attempts; climate-control-related dissatisfaction <=5% in post-test survey.
assumptions: Common quick tasks are defined consistently for test participants (temperature change, fan speed, windshield defog).
Combination of physical and software-based quick controls will be evaluated as solutions.
uncertainties: Different users may prefer different control modalities (touch vs tactile knobs); multiple valid solutions may be necessary.
drafts.scope_reason: Climate control usability is a customer-facing requirement appropriate for successor development.

drafts.title: Deliver predictable, confident braking feel and strong stopping performance
drafts.description: Drivers experience a linear and predictable brake pedal feel and confident stopping performance across speeds and load conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In objective brake testing, 100–0 km/h stopping distance must be <=38 meters under standard test conditions, and in driver feedback tests >=85% rate braking predictability top-2 on a 5-point scale.
assumptions: Standard test conditions align with current BMW brake test protocols and representative tire selections.
Stopping-distance target balances NVH, regenerative braking characteristics and customer expectations.
uncertainties: Braking feel is influenced by brake-by-wire and regenerative blending choices which may require calibration trade-offs.
Wet or icy conditions will affect absolute stopping distances; targets apply to dry standard test surfaces.
drafts.scope_reason: Braking performance and pedal feel are direct customer-experience outcomes to be retained or improved.

drafts.title: Improve interior storage usability to accommodate common items
drafts.description: Customers have convenient, stable places to store everyday items (phones, tablets, water bottles) so they feel the cabin is practical.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The cabin must provide at least one enclosed compartment that fits a 12-inch tablet flat, two vertical 850 ml bottles in dedicated holders, and a wireless-phone area that secures devices during cornering; in a user study >=80% rate storage convenience top-2.
assumptions: Typical water-bottle sizes among target customers are ~850 ml for large bottles; tablet sizes reflect common 11–13 inch devices.
Test includes dynamic stability checks to ensure items remain secure during normal driving maneuvers.
uncertainties: New phone form factors and oversized cases could affect wireless-phone area fit; flexible design may be beneficial.
drafts.scope_reason: Improving interior storage is a pragmatic, customer-facing requirement for the successor vehicle.

drafts.title: Offer enhanced ambient lighting customization and a panoramic glass roof option
drafts.description: Customers can personalize cabin ambiance with richer ambient lighting choices and can opt for a panoramic glass roof that increases daylight feeling while providing sun protection.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting must offer at least 10 distinct color palettes selectable by the user and personalization scenes; when the panoramic glass roof option is selected, >=80% of users in a daylight study must report improved spatial impression/top-2 on a 5-point scale while the glass and sunshade system limit cabin solar heating impact to a level comparable to a closed opaque roof in at least 70% of sunny-day tests.
assumptions: Color palettes and scenes are meaningful to customers and implemented in a way that avoids distracting transitions.
Panoramic roof option includes an effective sunshade (manual or automatic) and coatings to reduce solar heat gain.
uncertainties: Exact thermal performance will depend on glazing technology availability and may affect cost and weight trade-offs.
Some customers may prefer a solid roof for thermal or acoustic reasons; offering as an option helps address this.
drafts.scope_reason: Ambient lighting and roof configuration are customer-facing feature choices for the successor vehicle.

drafts.title: Improve voice recognition accuracy and onboard hotspot reliability
drafts.description: Customers can use natural-language voice commands reliably while driving, and the in-car WiFi hotspot provides stable connectivity for passengers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Voice recognition success rate for natural-language driver commands in US English must be >=90% in real-road noise conditions across a representative command set; the vehicle WiFi hotspot must deliver at least 5 Mbps per connected device for 90% of measured trips in typical suburban/highway routes.
assumptions: Voice models are localized for US English and tuned for in-cabin noise profiles; hotspot performance depends on available cellular networks.
Measured trips reflect typical customer usage patterns and carrier coverage in target markets.
uncertainties: Cellular network variability and carrier policies could affect hotspot consistency; partnerships with carriers may mitigate this.
Voice recognition performance can degrade with accented speech or simultaneous multi-speaker scenarios.
drafts.scope_reason: Improving voice control usability and hotspot reliability are direct customer experience improvements planned for the successor vehicle.
